contentBlocks.body: A Set stores each value only once. When you need unique tags, completed lesson ids, or visited pages, a Set is clearer than manually checking an array over and over.

contentBlocks.code:
const tags = new Set(["js", "arrays", "js"]);
const uniqueTags = [...tags]; // ["js", "arrays"]

contentBlocks.body: **Worked example.** A Set stores each distinct primitive value once and iterates in insertion order. The second b is already present, so it adds no new entry. Spreading converts the Set back to an array.
Two different objects with identical fields are still different Set entries because object equality uses identity.

**Try a small change.** How would you deduplicate objects by their id instead?

payload.explanation: A Set contains unique values, so repeated primitive values are stored once.
